# A deleted spec whose subject stayed must name it in the retirement account

Refs #17922 · sibling of #17924

## Context

#17922 AC-4 asks the guard to "close the class, not just the instance". This is that leaf: #17924 restored the 21 specs that came back verbatim, and this makes the deletion that lost them mechanically observable next time.

`buildScripts/util/check-spec-retirement.mjs` already existed when `c623b2f63c` deleted 796 unit specs, and it **passed correctly**. Its documented contract — settled deliberately when the guard was authored — is that an account must EXIST, never that it is TRUE:

> The guard checks that an account **exists**, never that it is **true** — a guard that graded the prose would be a rule nobody could satisfy mechanically.

That reasoning is sound and this ticket does not challenge it. But it means the guard's protection is exactly as strong as the account's honesty, and one sentence was allowed to account for 796 deletions.

## The Problem

One half of "true" is not prose at all.

Nothing can grade "folded into `X`". But **"the subject of this deleted spec is still in this repository"** is a fact about the tree, not a claim about intent — and it is precisely the half `c623b2f63c` got wrong.

Measured against the tree that commit itself produced, not against `dev` today:

| population | count |
|---|---|
| unit specs deleted by `c623b2f63c` | 796 |
| ...whose subject **still resolved** in that same tree | **34** |
| ...of those 34, named anywhere in the account | **0** |

The account described all 796 as Brain-owned coverage leaving with Agent OS. For 34 of them the implementation never left.

**Two of those 34 rows are new information, not a restatement of #17922.** That ticket censused `test/playwright/unit/ai/buildScripts/**` by hand and found 27 surviving subjects. This instrument sees 22 of those 27 (bound stated below) — and **12 more that nothing had censused**, all under `src/ai/**`, all with implementations still present at `HEAD` today and no unit coverage:

```
src/ai/LockRegistry.mjs          src/ai/client/ComponentService.mjs
src/ai/TransactionService.mjs    src/ai/client/DockService.mjs
src/ai/WriteGuard.mjs            src/ai/client/InstanceService.mjs
src/ai/admitWrite.mjs            src/ai/client/RuntimeService.mjs
src/ai/deriveSubtreePath.mjs     src/ai/client/TourRunner.mjs
src/ai/parseAgentEnvelope.mjs    src/ai/resolveWriteLock.mjs
```

#17922 explicitly scoped those out ("the other 774 deletions... this ticket makes no claim about them"). They are recorded here as a **finding**, not as scope: restoring them is neither this ticket nor #17922, and wants its own leaf.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/util/check-spec-retirement.mjs` — the guard. Pure exported functions plus a git-reading `collectViolations`; the spec imports the pure half and needs no repository.
- `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/checkSpecRetirement.spec.mjs` — its spec, one of the survivors of the split (it sat outside the `ai/` subtree that was swept).
- `.husky/pre-push` runs the guard; `.github/workflows/spec-retirement-lint.yml` runs it on `dev` PRs. Neither changes here.
- The guard reads `git ls-tree -r --name-only <sha>` — the tree the deleting commit **produced**. Not `HEAD`: the question is whether the subject survived *that deletion*, which keeps the rule deterministic and replayable over history.

## The Fix

A second, narrower violation class beside the existing one. A commit that (a) has an account, (b) deletes a unit spec, and (c) does not mention the implementation that stayed, is reported — naming any one candidate path discharges the row.

- `deriveSubjectSuffix(specPath)` → `<parentDir>/<name>.mjs`
- `findSurvivingSubjects(specPath, treePaths)` → surviving subject paths, `test/` excluded
- `unaccountedSurvivors(specs, treePaths, message)` → the unnamed rows
- `formatSurvivingSubjectFailure(violations)` → the report

**The parent-directory affinity is measured, not stylistic, and it is the load-bearing design choice.** A bare basename rule was the first draft; replaying it over `c623b2f63c` produced **ten false positives** — four per-server `logger.spec.mjs` files resolving to `src/util/Logger.mjs`, two `Server.spec.mjs` files to `examples/form/field/fileupload/server.mjs`, `scheduling/picker.spec.mjs` to `src/form/field/Picker.mjs`. None is the deleted spec's subject. Demanding an account for a file the author never touched is what the guard's own header warns against: it trains people to route around the check.

So the rule **under-reports rather than over-reports, deliberately**. For an account-demanding guard a false positive is the expensive error and a missed row is merely the status quo.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unaccountedSurvivors` violation class | this ticket | a deleting commit that HAS an account must name each deleted spec's surviving subject; any one candidate path discharges the row | the existing no-account class is untouched and reported independently | function JSDoc | replay of `c623b2f63c` reds with 34 rows; the same commit with paths appended greens |
| `deriveSubjectSuffix` affinity rule | this ticket | subject resolves as `<parentDir>/<name>.mjs`, case-insensitive, `test/` excluded | under-reports where a subject's filename differs from its spec's; never over-reports | function JSDoc naming the ten measured collisions | all ten basename collisions dropped; 22 in-scope rows retained |
| account contract for genuinely departed subjects | the guard's existing contract | unchanged — free prose, no path required | n/a | function JSDoc | the three departed subjects stay green |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — this narrows a guard's own contract; no ADR governs the spec-retirement account shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Replaying `c623b2f63c` with its exact account reds, naming the deleted spec and the surviving subject per row. Shown green against the pre-change guard first.
- [ ] A deletion whose subjects genuinely left stays green — the rule narrows, never widens, what the marker must assert.
- [ ] The same commit with the surviving paths named in the account greens, so the rule is satisfiable rather than a veto.
- [ ] The ten measured basename collisions from `c623b2f63c` are not reported.
- [ ] Each new spec arm is shown red against a seeded mutation of its own subject — an arm that cannot fail is not coverage.
- [ ] The two violation classes are reported in one run rather than one-per-push.

## Out of Scope

- **Restoring the 12 `src/ai/**` specs this surfaced.** A finding here, not scope. It now has its own leaf and its own census: **#17968**, filed 2026-08-31 per RA-4 of @neo-gpt's review on PR #17965, so the finding stays in the live queue rather than living in this body.
- **The six residual specs of #17922.** Still owed on the parent, each with a named cause.
- **Grading the account's prose.** Rejected deliberately when the guard was authored, and still right — the mechanical half is subject *resolvability*, which is what this tests.
- **Making `spec-retirement-lint.yml` a required context.** #17171 owns required-context binding for all 19 `*-lint.yml` workflows.
- **Guards with no caller.** #17783 owns the enforcement axis.

## Avoided Traps

- **A repo-wide basename match.** Measured: ten false positives on the one commit this exists to catch. A guard that fires on files the author never touched gets routed around, and then protects nothing.
- **Reading `HEAD` instead of the deleting commit's own tree.** It would make the verdict drift with unrelated later commits and make history un-replayable.
- **Claiming this reproduces #17922's 27.** It sees 22. The five it cannot see have subjects whose filename differs from the spec's (`TicketIndex.spec.mjs` → `tickets.mjs`, `WorkflowConcurrency.spec.mjs` → a `.yml` file), which no mechanical name rule recovers. Stating the bound is the point; a guard that claimed the full 27 would be the same over-claim the ticket is about.
- **Requiring every candidate path.** The author is being asked to acknowledge the implementation stayed, not to enumerate every file sharing a name.

Structure-map gate: N/A — no new or relocated `.mjs`.

This ticket is filed to give that work an honest delivered close target rather than a bare `Refs` edge on the parent, which still owes six residual specs and cannot close.

Refs #17922"
- 2026-08-31T18:30:15Z @tobiu referenced in commit `a4f5997` - "fix(build): the guard read an unreadable tree as a clean one (#17964)

RA-1/2/3 from @neo-gpt on PR #17965, and all three were in the consumed path
rather than in a helper — which is why helper-level green certified nothing.

The tree read failed OPEN. `git ls-tree -r --name-only` over this repository
emits 1,327,472 bytes against node's 1 MB default `maxBuffer`; the overrun threw
ENOBUFS, `tryExec` swallowed it, and the surviving-subject scan graded every
commit against an EMPTY tree — in which nothing has ever survived. Measured: the
guard saw 0 tracked paths and reported 0 rows. Raising the ceiling alone would
not fix it, because the defect is not the size: an unreadable tree and a clean
one returned the same value. So the ceiling moves to 64 MB AND the read refuses,
on the same reasoning the range read already used.

The ACCOUNT must name the survivor, not the message. The search ran over the
whole commit body, so a path in the headline, a rationale, or a `Refs:` trailer
discharged an account that named nothing — `refactor: rework <path>` plus a
generic `spec-retired: moved to Brain` was accepted. Only `spec-retired:`
payloads are searched now.

Ambiguous affinity no longer invents a survivor, and the interesting half is that
a candidate COUNT cannot see it. This tree really is ambiguous for real suffixes
— portal `content/Component.mjs` has 2 candidates, `button/Base.mjs` 2,
draggable `toolbar/SortZone.mjs` 3 — but delete `src/functional/button/Base.mjs`
with its spec and the two collapse to one: `src/button/Base.mjs`, a different
component the author never touched, now reading as unambiguous. Post-deletion the
tree cannot distinguish a departed subject from one that was never there. The
commit's own deleted paths can, so they are consulted first; the count rule stays
as the second guard.

Both defects are now reachable by test. `collectViolations` takes an injectable
git port and is exported, and the incident commit c623b2f63c replays through it
to exactly 34 rows — the same 34 the helper-level analysis found, and the ones
the fail-open read could not see. ~1.4s, reading history every clone already has.
`buildReports` is split out of `main` so an `if`->`else if` aggregation
regression is observable.

The false-positive arm carries its own vacuity control: drop the deleted-path
evidence and it fires again, which is what the guard did before this commit."

* test(ai): port the two behavioural arms across the v13.2 wire rename (#17968)

Both arms held red in the prior commit rather than silenced, because the choice
between 'assertion is stale' and 'subject has a defect' needed analysis. It is
the former, and the analysis names why.

ROOT CAUSE, for the diffDockTopology arm — not a rename, a silent walk halt.
The recovered fixtures carry pre-cut zone descriptors:

    root: {type: 'edge-zone', zones: {center: 'main-split'}}   // bare string

`Document.getZoneNodeId()` returns a nodeId only for a record carrying a string
`nodeId`; a bare string yields null. So `TopologyDiff.indexItemLocations` walked
to root, resolved the centre zone to null, and stopped — indexing ZERO items on
both sides. The differ then reported no moves and no errors, because a document
with no reachable items genuinely has no diff. The subject is right; the fixture
addressed a shape that no longer exists.

That is also why this arm could not be fixed by reading the failure: 'expected 1
move, got 0' points at move detection, and the defect was two layers up in zone
resolution.

AC-4 — assertion/fixture changes, each with why the new form is correct:

1. zones: {center: 'x'} -> {center: {nodeId: 'x'}}  (DockService, TourRunner)
   The record form is what getZoneNodeId accepts and what every current fixture
   uses. Restores traversal; asserts nothing new.
2. schema 'neo.harness.dockZone.v1' -> 'neo.dock.zone.v1'
3. windowFingerprint 'neo.harness.dockShape.v1' -> 'neo.dock.shape.v1'
4. windowFingerprint 'neo.harness.dockTopologyShape.v1' -> 'neo.dock.topologyShape.v1'
   (2-4) The v13.2 cut renamed the neo.harness.* wire family to neo.dock.*
   (#17837 / PR #17841, landed 2026-08-29). Assertions updated, producers
   untouched — these arms exist to prove the fingerprint comes from Persistence,
   and the schema string is how they prove it.

DELIBERATELY NOT RENAMED: the corrupt fixture at :616 keeps
'neo.harness.dockLayout.v2'. Its invalidity is the point — the arm asserts a
non-validating surface still fails the restore closed. Renaming it to a valid
schema would weaken the test into passing for the wrong reason.

* test(ai): the wire-rename note describes behaviour, not its tracking refs (#17968)

The ticket-archaeology guard is right: durable comments must describe what the
code does, and a comment citing the tickets that renamed a wire family rots the
moment those close or get renumbered. The justification belongs in the PR body
and the commit that made the change, where both already carry it.

Rewritten to state the behaviour — the shipped family is `neo.dock.*`, the arm
proves the fingerprint is produced by Persistence rather than assembled by the
caller — with no ticket refs.

Third time this guard has caught me tonight, and always the same shape: I cite
the ticket while JUSTIFYING a change, in the comment rather than the commit.
